section_summary: A newspaper clipping reports plans to expand Japanese radio broadcasting, including new transmitters, local stations, and foreign-language programming. State Department correspondence requests details about the proposed stations and a planned broadcasting association meeting, then follows up when no reply is found. The section ends with a brief internal routing note.

people.name: Moore
people.role: Signed the November 1940 letter for the Secretary of State

people.name: RCR
people.role: Addressee of the internal routing note

subfiles.title: Radio to Be Expanded
subfiles.about: Reports planned transmitters, local stations, expanded foreign broadcasts, and a regional radio meeting.
subfiles.summary: The Broadcasting Corporation of Japan plans two 100-kilowatt transmitters, nine local stations, more foreign-language programming, and a coordination meeting in Taihoku.

subfiles.title: Request for Information on Japanese Broadcasting Expansion
subfiles.to: Stanley G. Bravene, American Consul, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests technical and programming details of proposed transmitters and information on the Far Eastern Broadcasting Association.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the consul’s October 8 despatch and asks for station frequencies, opening dates, directional antennas, intended audiences, and details of the planned Taihoku meeting.

subfiles.title: Follow-up on Proposed Broadcasting Stations and Association
subfiles.to: Stanley G. Bravene, American Consul, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Seeks a reply to the Department’s earlier inquiry about Japanese broadcasting plans.
subfiles.summary: Finding no reply to its November 12 instruction, the Department asks the consul to obtain available information discreetly.

subfiles.title: Internal Request for Files
subfiles.about: Requests that files 894.06/29 and 894.06/34 be sent to the writer.
subfiles.summary: Asks RCR to send the referenced files.
